articles.title: Make the acceptance condition executable
articles.subject: ESS & agentic engineering
articles.deck: Turn “looks right” into a condition you can inspect.
articles.description: One independent acceptance predicate, a runnable example, and a counterexample.
source_refs: Hearth & Code ESS public-spec manuscript candidate 2, section 12: transition guards

articles.title: Treat prompt fields as data, not separators
articles.subject: Prompt craft
articles.deck: A delimiter is part of the data eventually. Choose framing that survives the data you expect.
articles.description: Test whether a prompt transport preserves items that contain its separator.

articles.title: Check output shape before the next step
articles.subject: Agentic engineering
articles.deck: A result can be plausible text and still be unusable data. Validate the shape before consuming it.
articles.description: Reject missing fields and wrong item types before a downstream operation reads an output.

articles.title: Keep a simple baseline in the comparison
articles.subject: Evaluation practice
articles.deck: A candidate is easier to interpret when the comparison target is visible and simple enough to audit.
articles.description: Compare declared numeric criteria with a baseline and an explicit margin.

articles.title: Stop refinement at a declared budget
articles.subject: Agentic engineering
articles.deck: Refinement is useful until its cost and stopping rule disappear. Make the budget part of the trace.
articles.description: Verify that a refinement trace stays within its iteration budget and records one entry per iteration.

articles.title: Carry the constraints across a handoff
articles.subject: Agentic engineering
articles.deck: A handoff is a new boundary. Compare the receiving brief with the constraints that made the original task meaningful.
articles.description: Check that required and optional task constraints survive a synthetic handoff.

articles.title: Score a creative candidate with declared criteria
articles.subject: Creative practice
articles.deck: Arithmetic can expose a brief fit or threshold while leaving aesthetic judgement with the human reviewer.
articles.description: Apply explicit weighted criteria to a synthetic creative candidate without calling the score a quality verdict.

articles.title: Vary one creative parameter at a time
articles.subject: Creative practice
articles.deck: Isolate a change so the comparison has a chance to teach you what changed.
articles.description: Compare two synthetic creative candidates and require exactly one declared parameter to differ.

articles.title: Separate the fixed brief from optional variation
articles.subject: Creative practice
articles.deck: Give exploration room by naming what cannot move and what may move.
articles.description: Check that a synthetic creative candidate keeps fixed brief fields and uses only declared optional fields and values.

articles.title: Choose a diverse concept set with declared tags
articles.subject: Creative practice
articles.deck: Diversity is not a mood word. Declare the tags and coverage floor you intend to preserve.
articles.description: Check a synthetic concept set for unique identities, required tags and a declared diversity floor.

articles.title: Check design contrast with the WCAG formula
articles.subject: Design with AI
articles.deck: Put the contrast calculation beside the palette decision so a readable design is testable before it is polished.
articles.description: Calculate relative luminance and compare a synthetic color pair with a declared contrast threshold.
source_refs: W3C Technique G18, contrast ratio procedure

articles.title: Detect source revision drift with explicit identity
articles.subject: Knowledge & synthesis
articles.deck: Compare the source identity you expected with the identity you actually received.
articles.description: A small explicit check for source revision drift without treating a version label as cryptographic proof.

source_refs.title: MDN Web Docs — JavaScript equality operators

articles.title: Require every claim to name its evidence
articles.subject: Knowledge & synthesis
articles.deck: Make support visible one claim at a time before synthesis hides the gaps.
articles.description: A claim-to-evidence checker that rejects claims with no named supporting record.

articles.title: Separate contradiction from missing evidence
articles.subject: Knowledge & synthesis
articles.deck: A gap in support and a conflict in support require different next moves.
articles.description: Classify unsupported records separately from records that assert incompatible values for the same claim.

articles.title: Preserve minority conclusions during synthesis
articles.subject: Knowledge & synthesis
articles.deck: A synthesis can report agreement without erasing a material dissent.
articles.description: A retention check that keeps every supplied conclusion, including minority positions, in a synthesis record.

articles.title: Detect cycles in a dependency graph
articles.subject: Knowledge & synthesis
articles.deck: A plan that depends on itself cannot be ordered by waiting harder.
articles.description: Use depth-first traversal to identify a directed dependency cycle before scheduling work.

articles.title: Select context by relevance under a token budget
articles.subject: Knowledge & synthesis
articles.deck: Make the selection rule visible when the context window cannot hold everything.
articles.description: A deterministic greedy selector that prioritizes relevance while keeping within a declared token budget.

articles.title: Preserve source offsets when extracting spans
articles.subject: Knowledge & synthesis
articles.deck: Record the index unit or a quotation can no longer be reliably re-located.
articles.description: Check extracted spans against JavaScript UTF-16 code-unit offsets, including surrogate-pair boundaries.

articles.title: Explain a revision with set differences
articles.subject: Knowledge & synthesis
articles.deck: Say what entered and left a revision before narrating why it changed.
articles.description: Use added and removed set members to give a compact, reproducible revision explanation.

articles.title: Separate evidence confidence from release status
articles.subject: Knowledge & synthesis
articles.deck: A well-supported claim can still be a draft, and a released item is not a confidence score.
articles.description: Keep evidence confidence and release lifecycle in independent fields rather than deriving one from the other.

articles.title: Reject stale retrieval evidence at an explicit boundary
articles.subject: Knowledge & synthesis
articles.deck: Freshness is a comparison between a recorded retrieval time and a declared limit.
articles.description: Reject evidence that exceeds a stated maximum age while accepting the exact boundary.

articles.title: Fail closed when a guard state is unknown
articles.subject: ESS & agentic engineering
articles.deck: Preserve the current state when the condition for moving cannot be evaluated.
articles.description: A tri-state guard checker that treats unknown as a hold with visible evidence.

articles.title: Keep capability separate from permission
